(Sl.No. 3004)
Court No. - 79
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 27261 of 2019
Applicant :- Rohit Chaudhari And 3 Ors

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.Wives and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Hitesh Pachori,Pintu Tiwari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ram Bahadur Hon'ble Anish Kumar Gupta,J.
1. Heard Sri Hitesh Pachori, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Anil Srivastava, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Sri Ram Bahadur, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 and Ms. Ruchi Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

The instant application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed seeking quashing of the entire criminal proceedings of Complaint Case No. 6371 of 2018 (Smt. Manisha vs. Rohit Chaudhari and others) under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.-Fatehpur Sikri,
District-Agra as well as summoning order dated 29.03.2019.

sentences.text: At the outset, learned counsel for the applicants submits that since the applicant no. 4 was not summoned by the trial court, therefore, he may be permitted to delete the name of applicant no. 4 from the array of parties.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants is permitted to carry out the necessary correction in the memo of parties and the name of applicant no.4 be deleted from the array of parties.

5. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the instant complaint case for the offence under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. has been filed by the opposite party no.2 alleging therein that the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no.2 were married on 27.11.2015 as per Hindu rites and customs with pomp and show.
Subsequent to the marriage, the applicants herein used to torture and harass the opposite party no. 2 for demand of additional dowry of Rs. 10,00,000/-.
Due to non-fulfillment of the aforesaid amount of dowry, the applicants used to abuse her and torture her mentally and physically.
It is alleged that the applicants no. 2, 3 as well as applicant no. 4 had beaten the opposite party no. 2 on 06.05.2017 whereby the opposite party no. 2 sustained internal injuries.

It is further alleged that all the jewellery etc., were already taken in possession by the applicants no.
2 and 3 and has not been returned to the opposite party no.2.
6.

With the aforesaid allegation, the instant complaint has been filed on 16.10.2018 by the opposite party no. 2 and in support of her complaint, the statement of the complainant was recorded under Section 200 Cr.P.C. as well as statements of witnesses, namely, Sangram Singh and Lakhan Singh was recorded under Section 202 Cr.P.C.

On the basis of the aforesaid allegations and the statements recorded under Section 200 and 202 Cr.P.C., the trial court has found a prima facie case against the applicants and has summoned them for trial vide impugned order dated 29.03.2019, against which the instant application has been filed by the applicants.

7. Vide order dated 16.7.2019, the matter was referred to the Mediation Centre, however, as per the report received from the Mediation Centre, despite the presence of opposite party no.2, applicants never appeared before the Mediation Centre.
Therefore, the mediation centre could not proceed further in the matter and the mediation between the parties was unsuccessful.

8. Learned counsel for the applicants relying upon the communication sent by the opposite party no.2 to the President, Air Force Wives Welfare Association dated 23.10.2017 submits that till the filing of such application on 23.10.2017, there is not a single allegation that the opposite party no. 2 was being harassed for any demand of dowry rather the allegation is that the applicants used filthy language against her for non-performing the daily household chores or not cooking the food as per their desire.
However, no cruelty of any kind except she was asked to do the entire domestic work in the house has been alleged in the letter dated 23.10.2017.
However, in the instant complaint, it has been alleged that soon after the marriage, the applicants were demanding Rs. 10,00,000/- as additional dowry and for the same they used to torture her.

Therefore, learned counsel for the applicants submits that from both the aforesaid letters read with the complaint, it is apparent that the cause of matrimonial discord was other than any demand of dowry rather the opposite party no.
2 was unhappy doing the domestic work as the applicant no. 1 used to be on his duty at the Air Force, which was the main cause of matrimonial discord.

Therefore, no offence whatsoever as Rohit Chaudhari And 3 Ors vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97881015/
2 alleged is made out against the applicants.

sentences.text: 9. So far as the allegation with regard to giving of gifts at the time of marriage is concerned, in paragraph 2 of the complaint, there is no allegation that any such amount or article was given on demand rather it appears to have been given by the family members of the opposite party no. 2 out of their sweet will as gifts in the marriage.

Therefore, learned counsel for the applicants submits that from the material on record, no offence whatsoever is made out against the applicants, hence, he seeks quashing of the entire proceedings of the instant case.

10. Per contra, learned Senior Advocate for the opposite party no. 2 submits that the letters which were written to the President, Air Force Wives Welfare Association by the opposite party no. 2 were written only for the purpose of getting maintenance and since those officers were not competent to decide the allegations with regard to cruelty, no allegations were made in those letters.

However,
when those letters were sent to the officers, so that the matrimonial relationship between the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no. 2 may be mended.

Learned Senior Counsel further submits that when the applicants did not mend their ways, the instant complaint case has been filed by the opposite party no. 2, which is duly supported by the statement of witnesses.

Therefore, a prima facie case is made out against the applicants and no interference is called for while exercising the jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
11.

Learned A.G.A. also supports the submissions made by learned Senior Counsel for the opposite party no. 2.
12.
Having heard the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court has carefully gone through the records of the case.

13. From the reading of the complaint, specifically paragraph 2 wherein various articles and the amounts stated to have been spent by the parents of the opposite party no. 2, appears to have been given by the parents of the opposite party no. 2 out of their sweet will without there being any allegation of any demand made by the applicants.
Therefore, by no stretch of imagination, the same can be stated to be dowry for the purposes of prosecution of the applicants.

Though in the subsequent paragraphs the allegations have been made with regard to demand of dowry of Rs.
10,00,000/-, however, if we look into the definition of 'Dowry' in Section 2 of the D.P. Act, dowry means any property or valuable security given or agreed to be given in connection with the marriage.
In the instant case, this demand of Rs. 10,00,000/- neither has been given nor has been agreed to be given, so by no stretch of imagination, it can be said to be dowry.
Therefore, in the considered opinion of this Court, no offence under the provisions of the D.P. Act would be attracted in the instant case.

14. So far as the cruelty regarding demand of money is concerned, from reading of the letters earlier written by the opposite party no. 2 to the President, Air Force Wives Welfare Association, it appears that no such demand or harassment subjected to opposite party no. 2 for any demand of dowry rather the harassment alleged in the said letters was only for non-performance of the domestic chores to the satisfaction of the applicants.

Therefore, the same cannot be covered within the Rohit Chaudhari And 3 Ors vs State Of U.P. And Another on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97881015/
3 meaning of Section 498A I.P.C.

sentences.text: Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court, the instant complaint case is nothing but a misuse of process of law by the opposite party no. 2 by making false and concocted allegations, therefore, the same cannot survive.

15. For the reasons aforesaid, the instant application is allowed and the entire proceedings of Complaint Case No. 6371 of 2018 (Smt. Manisha vs. Rohit Chaudhari and others) under Section 498A, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, P.S.-Fatehpur Sikri, District-Agra are hereby quashed.
